title: P1-7r compiler-aliases: Add Save + Set match arm in part_02.rs canonical lowering (digest identity)
description: Feature P1-7r (revision of black-hat-revised vb-ljxig). Black-hat review round 1 scoped this work to the Save match arm in the canonical lowering path, since 'save' and 'set' are both parsed in crates/vb_compile/src/ast/parse.rs:271-274 but the canonical lowering match in crates/vb_compile/src/mod_compile_lowering/part_02.rs:28-130 only handles Set (line 29) — the Save arm is missing and falls to the `other =>` arm (line 131) returning UnsupportedStepPrimitive. The black-hat verified that the Do arm IS present at part_02.rs:95-130 and the Set arm is at part_02.rs:29, so we only need to add Save. Real source: part_02.rs:18-140 (lower_canonical_step), part_05.rs:374 (StepPrimitive::Save { value } — the reference handling), part_08.rs:210 (StepPrimitive::Set | StepPrimitive::Save => compile_save — the non-canonical path). The fix: (1) add `StepPrimitive::Save { output, value } =>` arm in part_02.rs:29 that calls lower_canonical_set (since Save and Set have identical semantics, just different YAML keywords); (2) ensure the digest computation treats Save and Set identically (the digest code is in part_05.rs:101: StepPrimitive::Save { .. } => 'save' — and the corresponding code in part_05.rs:374 reads the value). Master §16.4 alias convention: save and set are aliases for the same Set primitive; do and run are aliases for the same Do primitive. Kani harness: prove save_and_set_produce_identical_digests on the same value. proptest: 100 random (save, set) pairs produce identical workflows.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL accept both 'save' and 'set' YAML keywords in the canonical lowering path
THE SYSTEM SHALL produce identical digests for `save: { output: x, value: 42 }` and `set: { output: x, value: 42 }`

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a workflow YAML contains `save: { output: x, value: 42 }`
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL lower it to a Set node, identical to `set: { output: x, value: 42 }`

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a workflow YAML contains `set: { output: x, value: 42 }` (existing path)
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL lower it to a Set node (preserved behavior)

unwanted.condition: IF the user provides both `save` and `set` in the same step (impossible in YAML by design)
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT emit a non-None action_id, mock_output, or suspension_reason for Set or Finish steps
unwanted.because: Each step has exactly one primitive key
